text:
I've handled the S-107 delay. I ordered the missing 600 cartons from the backup supplier, S-114, and notified the five contracted health systems at DC-EAST. Wholesaler notices and alternative-product guidance are handed to the right teams. **I recorded no allocation:** the only packs below safety stock are covered by the backup supplier. There was no approved playbook, so I followed the Supply Disruption Response process steps.

## What I found
- **The late order:** S-107 (Glenwood Cartons) has 4 open orders for CMP-530 (a folding carton). The next one, PO001160, is 600 units promised to ship 2026-10-03. Four weeks late puts it around 2026-10-31.
- **Products affected:** CMP-530 goes into the pack kit KIT-100, made at plant PL-01. The kit is used in:
  - Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL, and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (made at PL-01);
  - Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (made at PL-02);
  - lens-care, surgical, supplement, diagnostic and antibiotic products made at plants PL-03 and PL-04. None of these is in the commercial database, and there is no DC stock record for them.
- **Backup supplier:** S-114 (Norland Paperboard) is qualified for CMP-530. The supplier portal shows it active and approved, but only for plant PL-01. S-107 is not on hold.
- **DC stock vs safety stock (snapshot 2026-09-25):**

| DC | Pack | On hand | Safety stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| DC-EAST | Lacrivia 5 mL | 46 | 471 |
| DC-EAST | Lacrivia 10 mL | 34 | 233 |

  Every other affected pack at every DC is at or above safety stock, including all Oculon packs.
- **Recovery time:** it takes 23 days from carton arrival to stock at the DC (transit, kitting, a 14-day sterility test, then shipping to the DC). Recovery is expected around 2026-11-15 if S-114's open order PO001178 ships on 2026-10-23, and around 2026-11-23 if S-107's late shipment arrives about 2026-10-31.
- **Substitutes:** none can be offered. The other Lacrivia pack is also below safety stock at DC-EAST, and Cyclosporine OS uses the same carton and kit. That leaves no company substitute, so Medical Affairs guides alternatives.
- **Why no allocation:** the rules only allow allocating packs the delay actually cuts off. The two short Lacrivia packs are made at PL-01, which S-114 can supply. Oculon isn't covered by S-114, but it is above safety stock everywhere.

## Actions taken
| Step | Action | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Backup supply | Purchase requisition to S-114 for 600 CMP-530, ship to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-06, marked expedite | PR-CFEC4687 |
| Account teams | Riverbend AC00059 (Tier A) | CRM-D31011C9 |
| | Oak Hollow AC00038 (Tier A) | CRM-372E052D |
| | Northfield AC00117 (Tier A) | CRM-9AE3B6F7 |
| | Clearview AC00001 (Tier B) | CRM-6D7C2D84 |
| | Sunridge AC00138 (Tier B) | CRM-BBC23E26 |
| Wholesalers | Case for Trade Relations to notify W-01 Keystone and W-02 Atlas (the wholesaler messaging system has no connection) | CASE-2528FE50 |
| Alternatives | Case for Medical Affairs to advise on alternatives to Lacrivia | CASE-876DB7F3 |

Each account-team task says the account gets no allocation, gives the expected recovery date, and says no company substitute can be offered.

## Not done, and why
- **No allocation and no approval request:** nothing qualifies under the allocation rules, as explained above.
- **No direct messages to wholesalers:** the messaging system has no connection, so Trade Relations has it.
- **No transfer from DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST to DC-EAST:** both have spare Lacrivia stock, but a transfer needs the Supply Planning lead's approval and isn't part of this process. Raise it if you want one.

## Assumptions and risks
- **The backup order may not arrive sooner.** S-114 usually takes about 33 days from order to shipment, so the new order is only faster than S-107's late shipment if S-114 expedites it. Purchasing should confirm a ship date.
- **"Affected DC" means DC-EAST**, the only DC with an affected pack below safety stock. I only notified the five contracted health systems there (all have Lacrivia prescriptions at DC-EAST in the last 13 weeks). Accounts without a contract weren't notified.
- **Plant coverage:** I treated S-114 as covering packs made at PL-01, as the allocation rule is worded. Since the carton is only used at PL-01, either reading leads to the same result: no allocation.
- **DC-EAST was already short before this delay.** Lacrivia there was below safety stock while CENTRAL and WEST had plenty, so the shortage may come from how stock is spread across DCs, not only from the cartons.
- **The other products** using this carton (PL-03 and PL-04) have no DC stock or prescription data, so I couldn't check their exposure.

Knowledge-layer sources: process "Supply Disruption Response" (steps SDR-1.1 to 4.2), rules BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-CUST-01, BR-REGION-01 and BR-APPR-01, the supply exposure trace and lead times, and reference sets supply_contracts, dc_service_regions, approved_substitutes and list_prices.

CMP-530 supplier S-107 is delayed ~4 weeks; an alternate supplier has been requisitioned (PR-CFEC4687). Expected recovery at DC: ~2026-11-15 to 2026-11-23. question: Supplier S-107 will miss its next CMP-530 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I've handled the S-107 delay. I ordered the missing 600 cartons from the backup supplier, S-114, and notified the five contracted health systems at DC-EAST. Wholesaler notices and alternative-product guidance are handed to the right teams. **I recorded no allocation:** the only packs below safety stock are covered by the backup supplier. There was no approved playbook, so I followed the Supply Disruption Response process steps.

## What I found
- **The late order:** S-107 (Glenwood Cartons) has 4 open orders for CMP-530 (a folding carton). The next one, PO001160, is 600 units promised to ship 2026-10-03. Four weeks late puts it around 2026-10-31.
- **Products affected:** CMP-530 goes into the pack kit KIT-100, made at plant PL-01. The kit is used in:
  - Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL, and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (made at PL-01);
  - Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (made at PL-02);
  - lens-care, surgical, supplement, diagnostic and antibiotic products made at plants PL-03 and PL-04. None of these is in the commercial database, and there is no DC stock record for them.
- **Backup supplier:** S-114 (Norland Paperboard) is qualified for CMP-530. The supplier portal shows it active and approved, but only for plant PL-01. S-107 is not on hold.
- **DC stock vs safety stock (snapshot 2026-09-25):**

| DC | Pack | On hand | Safety stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| DC-EAST | Lacrivia 5 mL | 46 | 471 |
| DC-EAST | Lacrivia 10 mL | 34 | 233 |

  Every other affected pack at every DC is at or above safety stock, including all Oculon packs.
- **Recovery time:** it takes 23 days from carton arrival to stock at the DC (transit, kitting, a 14-day sterility test, then shipping to the DC). Recovery is expected around 2026-11-15 if S-114's open order PO001178 ships on 2026-10-23, and around 2026-11-23 if S-107's late shipment arrives about 2026-10-31.
- **Substitutes:** none can be offered. The other Lacrivia pack is also below safety stock at DC-EAST, and Cyclosporine OS uses the same carton and kit. That leaves no company substitute, so Medical Affairs guides alternatives.
- **Why no allocation:** the rules only allow allocating packs the delay actually cuts off. The two short Lacrivia packs are made at PL-01, which S-114 can supply. Oculon isn't covered by S-114, but it is above safety stock everywhere.

## Actions taken
| Step | Action | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Backup supply | Purchase requisition to S-114 for 600 CMP-530, ship to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-06, marked expedite | PR-CFEC4687 |
| Account teams | Riverbend AC00059 (Tier A) | CRM-D31011C9 |
| | Oak Hollow AC00038 (Tier A) | CRM-372E052D |
| | Northfield AC00117 (Tier A) | CRM-9AE3B6F7 |
| | Clearview AC00001 (Tier B) | CRM-6D7C2D84 |
| | Sunridge AC00138 (Tier B) | CRM-BBC23E26 |
| Wholesalers | Case for Trade Relations to notify W-01 Keystone and W-02 Atlas (the wholesaler messaging system has no connection) | CASE-2528FE50 |
| Alternatives | Case for Medical Affairs to advise on alternatives to Lacrivia | CASE-876DB7F3 |

Each account-team task says the account gets no allocation, gives the expected recovery date, and says no company substitute can be offered.

## Not done, and why
- **No allocation and no approval request:** nothing qualifies under the allocation rules, as explained above.
- **No direct messages to wholesalers:** the messaging system has no connection, so Trade Relations has it.
- **No transfer from DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST to DC-EAST:** both have spare Lacrivia stock, but a transfer needs the Supply Planning lead's approval and isn't part of this process. Raise it if you want one.

## Assumptions and risks
- **The backup order may not arrive sooner.** S-114 usually takes about 33 days from order to shipment, so the new order is only faster than S-107's late shipment if S-114 expedites it. Purchasing should confirm a ship date.
- **"Affected DC" means DC-EAST**, the only DC with an affected pack below safety stock. I only notified the five contracted health systems there (all have Lacrivia prescriptions at DC-EAST in the last 13 weeks). Accounts without a contract weren't notified.
- **Plant coverage:** I treated S-114 as covering packs made at PL-01, as the allocation rule is worded. Since the carton is only used at PL-01, either reading leads to the same result: no allocation.
- **DC-EAST was already short before this delay.** Lacrivia there was below safety stock while CENTRAL and WEST had plenty, so the shortage may come from how stock is spread across DCs, not only from the cartons.
- **The other products** using this carton (PL-03 and PL-04) have no DC stock or prescription data, so I couldn't check their exposure.

SELECT b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID, b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID, b.QTY_PER, b.EFF_FROM, b.EFF_TO, pm.PLANT_ID, m.MATERIAL_TYP FROM dbo.BOM b LEFT JOIN dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm ON pm.MATERIAL_ID=b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID WHERE (b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='CMP-530' OR (b.CHILD_MATERIAL_ID='KIT-100' AND b.PARENT_MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-2001','FG-2002'))) ORDER BY 1,2

latest AS (SELECT MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) AS dt FROM dbo.DC_INV)
SELECT pm.PLANT_ID, i.DC_ID, COUNT(*) AS n_fg_dc, SUM(CASE WHEN i.ON_HAND_UNITS < i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_below_ss, MAX(i.SNAPSHOT_DT) AS snap

WITH wks AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
acct AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, p.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) AS TOP_ID FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT p ON p.ACCOUNT_ID=a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON gp.ACCOUNT_ID=p.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT ac.TOP_ID, t.ACCOUNT_NM, r.PROD_NDC11, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) AS TRX13, MIN(w.WK_END_DT) wk_from, MAX(w.WK_END_DT) wk_to
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wks w ON w.WK_END_DT=r.WK_END_DT
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr ON pr.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN acct ac ON ac.ACCOUNT_ID=pr.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=ac.TOP_ID
WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') AND ac.STATE IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH')
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING SUM(r.TRX_QTY)>0 ORDER BY TRX13 DESC
